reviewed_feature_migrations.purpose: Reviewed Template 15 men-only booking guards and multi-service branch/unbranched booking RPC reconciliation; retained behind the protected manual production migration workflow.
Historical, comment-only compatibility marker for the per-salon Tawk widget migration chain; no DDL is applied by this file.
Historical, comment-only marker documenting the isolated widget_connections table; final DDL is consolidated in the reviewed 20261118203000 migration.

Reviewed per-salon Tawk.to live chat feature: creates private property_mappings and widget_connections prerequisites before ALTER/RPC DDL, enforces private RLS/service-role-only access, exposes only public widget IDs for published sites, and accepts the standard default widget ID. Retain behind the protected manual production migration workflow.

Role-level permissions: canonical staff access-role normalizer, server-side permission matrix mirroring src/lib/staffPermissions.ts, caller branch-role helper, and a pinned branch role CHECK constraint with legacy value normalization. Additive and read-only; no RLS policy is widened.
Staff invites, staff memberships and separate staff sign-in with hashed tokens and fail-closed grants.

Staff access hardening: explicit all_branches grant (empty branch scope now means no branch data), stale branch filtering on every read, atomic invite acceptance, reusable SECURITY DEFINER authorization helpers so RLS cannot recurse, and an owner-only RPC to change a live login's role/branch scope.

Fail-closed owner + branch-scoped staff RLS for branches, services and bookings, adapted to the real schema (branches.site_id, studioflow_services, studioflow_bookings): staff reads are scoped through studioflow_is_assigned_branch so a stranger or a branch-less login sees nothing, staff create/update bookings only inside their own branch and role (service providers read-only), and public catalogue reads are narrowed from a blanket is_active rule to bookable + published-salon rows. Customer CRM tables stay owner-only.

Column privacy for the public service catalogue: the table-wide SELECT grant to anon on public.services is replaced by explicit column grants that exclude owner_id, so a signed-out visitor can no longer read a salon's owner UUID. Row visibility still comes from services_public_read. The proposed security_invoker view was rejected because it depends on the very grant it revokes and therefore denies every anonymous read.

Storefront column privacy for the published-site catalogue: public_salon_websites projects only slug/content/published_at (never owner_id, the base table's primary key), anon loses its direct read of studioflow_websites, and studioflow_customer_catalog() is rewritten to project the view instead of embedding owner_id. Also stamps the public salon slug onto booking payloads via trigger + backfill so the customer app joins on slug rather than owner_id. The view is deliberately SECURITY DEFINER, the opposite of the public.services fix, because it exists to be readable by a role that cannot read the base table.
